messages:
maya: Quick Q for @auditor.jane and infra — auditor asked for evidence tying RBAC changes + ephemeral KMS usage to service-account rotation and incident trails for SOC2. Need an artifact list we can hand off.

auditor.jane: Hi Maya — please provide: 1) RoleBinding change log with actor/PR/time, 2) KMS CMK usage events (GenerateDataKey, Decrypt) around rotation windows, 3) STS/issuer events for service-account tokens, 4) SIEM-correlation showing these events linked to an incident id. CSV or zipped JSON preferred.

sam: We can pull RoleBinding audit from the k8s-audit-index in Splunk. Example search I'll run:
```splunk
index=k8s-audit source=kube_audit role_binding OR RoleBinding | sort 0 _time | table _time user verb objectRef.name requestURI | limit 200
```
I'll export as CSV.

ash: For KMS, CloudTrail has GenerateDataKey and Decrypt entries. Sample AWS CLI to pull events in the window:
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GenerateDataKey --start-time 2024-08-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2024-08-02T00:00:00Z --query Events --output json > generate_data_key_events.json
```
We should include the raw CloudTrail JSONs and an extracted CSV with eventTime, eventName, userIdentity.principalId, requestParameters.keyId, eventID.

leo: Note — our request tracing injects trace_id into X-Req-Id headers for inbound API calls and is propagated to the runtime. If we include examples showing trace_id in KMS events and in the SIEM incident, that demonstrates the chain. We log trace_id in ops-key-manager index as well.

maya: Auditor also asked for a demo proving revoked service accounts can't decrypt. Can infra run a playback: create temp creds, show decrypt success, revoke, then show decrypt failure? Short video or recorded logs are fine.

sam: Yep. I'll script a small repro runbook and record stdout. Steps: 1) create transient role and assume it 2) call GenerateDataKey/Encrypt 3) revoke role binding 4) retry Decrypt -> expect AccessDenied. I'll capture CloudTrail + Splunk lines.

auditor.jane: That works. Also attach retention policy proof: where logs are stored, retention durations (SOC2: typically 12 months), and any snapshot/manifests showing object creation dates. A simple CSV mapping control->artifact would be ideal.

ash: For retention: logs land in s3://redwood-audit-logs (retention 13 months, lifecycle -> Glacier after 90d). We'll include the bucket policy + lifecycle JSON and a small manifest of object keys used in exports.

maya: I'll compile a control mapping doc: control_id, artifact_name, path, collector, retention, notes. Will hand to auditor.

sam: Running Splunk export now for role changes and trace_id examples. Will upload to evidence bucket and post presigned link here when ready :thumbsup:

ci-bot: export job COMPLETE — s3://redwood-evidence/rotation-playback-1729543210.tar.gz (presigned placeholder) — checksum: sha256:abcd1234placeholder

maya: Thanks — auditor, I'll DM you the secure link + a CSV mapping and a short README describing artifacts and how to validate the playback.

auditor.jane: Thanks everyone. If you can include sample CloudTrail eventIDs and a couple of trace_ids mapped to the Splunk events, that will speed verification. I may request a one-hour remote session to walk the artifacts.

leo: I'll annotate two sample trace_ids in the export and include the Splunk search used to pull them.

maya: Great. Action items: sam export role-binding CSV + Splunk traces; ash export CloudTrail JSONs for GenerateDataKey/Decrypt; leo add trace_id mapping; sam record playback logs; maya assemble control->artifact CSV and DM auditor. I'll update this thread when uploads are done.
